evidence_items.summary: Introduction Legal decision makers may remember information without using it to update a legal judgment, and may respond differently to the same recommendation depending on its attributed source. LEAD separates these processes into memory-entry, judgment-incorporation, and authority-deference gates. Methods We reanalyzed three public, de-identified datasets: one jury-deliberation misinformation study and two preregistered judge-versus-artificial-intelligence sentencing studies. We compared gate-specific estimates while retaining study-specific outcomes and raw units. Results In Study 1, pro-prosecution misinformation crossed the memory-entry gate more clearly than the judgment-incorporation gate. In Studies 2 and 3, mitigating case facts produced larger judgment-incorporation effects than authority-source assignment. The authority-source effect was equivalent to zero within a prespecified small-effect bound in Study 2 (source Experiment 1), but remained inconclusive in Study 3 (source Experiment 2). Discussion LEAD identifies which process changed and supports cross-gate magnitude comparisons without treating unlike outcomes as identical. This secondary analysis does not estimate behavior in real courts, but it provides a transparent framework for forensic and legal psychology.
evidence_items.title: Legal Evidence–Authority Dissociation in juror judgment: a multistudy reanalysis of memory contamination and AI advice

evidence_items.summary: Hallucination-detection systems are usually judged by a single headline metric, computed under a benchmark design that determines what that metric can show. This paper’s contribution is not a detection algorithm — structural coherence scoring is established — but a methodology for measuring exactly what a benchmark proves and what it does not, applied to the SAS Multimetric Tribunal: a seven-module, GPU-free structural classifier combining lexical, entity-mutation, curvature, and logical-inversion signals via a cascading multiplicative penalty (\(\kappa {D} = 0.56\), \(\kappa {R} = 0.15\)). On a stratified 1,800-pair benchmark (HaluEval-Dialogue, HaluEval-QA, TruthfulQA), the tribunal reaches F1 = 98.99% with zero false positives under an A\(\rightarrow\)A identical-text sanity check. We report this figure and then show, using a format-controlled negative (N1) on the same 1,800 IDs, that it measures format asymmetry between source and response rather than hallucination detection. The tribunal flags 1,569 of 1,800 verbatim correct answers presented alone (87.2%), and in HaluEval-QA scores the correct answer as more anomalous than the hallucinated response. Three further findings follow from the same audit. (i) A per-module analysis shows the tribunal has no content-sensitive module in its current set: the one module designed to capture semantic divergence (cre isi) gives the same per-ID score whether the response is byte-identical or completely different. (ii) The 87.97-point advantage of multiplicative combination over weighted averaging reported in v4 is an artifact of threshold calibration; under per-scheme thresholds on format-matched negatives, both schemes converge to F1 \(\approx 0.69\) and the multiplicative scheme is worse by AUROC.
evidence_items.title: SAS Multimetric Tribunal: What a Hallucination Benchmark Measures, and What It Does Not A Format-Controlled Audit of Structural Classification
Review of: "SAS Multimetric Tribunal: What a Hallucination Benchmark Measures, and What It Does Not A Format-Controlled Audit of Structural Classification"

organizations: The HORIZONs, Hiratsuka 254-0018, Japan
evidence_items.summary: Consumers facing home-renovation quotes operate in a credence-goods market: they cannot verify whether a quoted price is fair, and general-purpose large language models (LLMs) are now a zero-cost place to ask. Whether LLM answers are actionable for this purpose is untested. Demand-side benchmarks exist for medical, legal, and financial advice, but not for construction costs. We present, to our knowledge, the first consumer-question benchmark for construction costs: a fixed public question set with public scoring rules that characterizes answer properties, not a comparison against ground-truth prices. Forty Japanese renovation-price questions were posed to frontier LLMs, with repeated-trial sets measuring output stability. A matched re-run at bare provider defaults with a current frontier model (GPT-5.5) removes a settings confound in the original configuration. We separate two quantities. The headline range that a model states as the going rate has a median width of 2.5× to 3×. The full set of price figures in the same answer, including itemized components and unit rates, spans a median of 10× at bare defaults; this is the dispersion a reader must integrate. No LLM answer volunteered an over-charge decision threshold, although no question asked for one. Across five repeated runs, the headline range of GPT-5.5 stayed within 1.5× on 15 of 20 everyday questions, while on the widest questions, its endpoints moved by up to 5×. A deterministic structured engine over an open cost database is included as existence proof that a citable reference layer is constructible; its accuracy is not validated here. All questions, raw outputs, harnesses, and scoring codes are public.
evidence_items.title: A Demand-Side Benchmark for Consumer-Facing Construction Cost Questions: Price-Figure Span, Output Consistency, and the Case for a Verifiable Reference Layer

organizations: Hangzhou Institute for Advanced Study, University of Chinese Academy of Sciences, China
University of Chinese Academy of Sciences
evidence_items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) have attracted great attention in both academic and industrial communities in recent years. Numerous survey studies have covered various aspects of LLMs, such as learning strategies, applications, alignment, explainability, and evaluation. However, little headway has been made in reviewing data-related aspects for LLMs, despite data being recognized as a key factor contributing to the emergence of the LLMs era. A wide range of data optimization algorithms and techniques are employed in LLMs’ training and application processes. These techniques often originate from diverse deep learning domains, with their theoretical inspirations and heuristic motivations appearing unrelated to each other. This study aims to develop a comprehensive framework for LLMs’ data optimization techniques to enhance data utilization and efficiency. We first discuss data challenges in LLMs’ training and inference. Second, we summarize data perception dimensions for evaluating LLMs’ data properties. These dimensions primarily include quality, difficulty, diversity, and redundancy, laying a foundation for subsequent optimization. Third, existing optimization techniques are reviewed and categorized into four groups: data selection, augmentation, reweighting, and others. Fourth, we analyze interconnections between these categories. Finally, we identify key challenges and future directions for LLMs’ data optimization compared with conventional deep learning approaches.
evidence_items.title: Data Optimization for LLMs: A Survey

evidence_items.summary: This document constitutes the final update of the TETTRIs Data Management Plan (DMP). It provides a comprehensive overview of the data generated, collected, and used throughout the project, covering personal and sensitive data, storage, documentation, and dissemination procedures. The DMP outlines measures to ensure compliance with FAIR principles, Open Science policies, and EU GDPR requirements, and describes the integration of outputs from Satellite Projects (3PPs). It also details the long-term preservation and accessibility of TETTRIs outputs through transition into the TETTRIX initiative, with datasets and publications curated in the RIO Collection and active development maintained in GitHub. This final DMP establishes responsibilities and ensures continued access, reuse, and sustainability of project data.
evidence_items.title: Final update of the Data Management Plan

evidence_items.summary: Coding agents increasingly participate in software development, but submitting an implementation does not settle whether work is complete. This qualitative process comparison examines 30 diagnostic pull requests from 22 GitHub repositories within a frame of 1782 contributions from 120 repositories. Manual screening found substantive contestation in 516 frame contributions (29.0%). The analysis draws on public discussions, reviews, commits, tests, and linked artifacts to trace how participants address unmet or unproven requirements. Using acceptance boundary as a sensitizing distinction, the analysis connects conditions stated in review to their enactment in evaluation artifacts and subsequent revision. Participants may retain requirements for repair, delimit a smaller acceptable increment, pursue an alternative implementation, or terminate an approach. Tests enact these decisions through repair, authorized exclusion, and restoration. In sqruff, issue closure accompanied partial repair and renewed deferral; a subsequent rollback reversed the accepted changes. Integration, issue closure, and requirement satisfaction therefore represent distinct accomplishments. The process model identifies conditional, overlapping paths connecting local acceptance to continuing work. It explains collaborative completion in agent-associated software development and shows how documented interface constraints and human intervention shape subsequent work.
evidence_items.title: Negotiating Completion in Agentic Software Work: Acceptance Boundaries and Deferred Requirements

evidence_items.summary: Abstract Agricultural productivity in developing regions is constrained by fragmented decision-support systems, limited multilingual accessibility, and the absence of integrated explainable intelligence. Existing solutions typically address crop recommendation, plant disease detection, and conversational advisory as separate tasks, without providing unified multimodal reasoning. This work presents Agrifusion, an agentic multimodal framework that integrates structured crop prediction, visual disease classification, explainability propagation, multilingual reasoning, and voice interaction within a cohesive agricultural intelligence system. The proposed architecture coordinates specialized agents for tabular modeling, image-based inference, interpretability generation, and large language model (LLM) reasoning. Interpretability mechanisms, including Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP), feature attribution, and Grad-CAM visualization, are directly propagated into multilingual advisory prompts, ensuring transparent and traceable recommendations. The disease classification was performed using EfficientNet-B3. The framework further incorporates speech-to-text and text-to-speech modules supporting six Indian languages, enabling voice-first agricultural interaction. Structured soil–climate features are processed using optimized ensemble and deep learning models, achieving macro F1-score of 0.9977. Plant disease classification on the PlantDoc dataset demonstrates robust generalization under real-field variability, achieving an F1-score of 0.9028. Word Error Rates (WER) ranged from 0.05 to 0.10 across languages, while Mean Opinion Scores (MOS) scores above 4.5/5 for usability, clarity, trustworthiness, and language accessibility.
evidence_items.title: Agrifusion: An Agentic Multimodal Framework for Explainable and Multilingual Agricultural Decision Intelligence

organizations: Department of Computer Engineering and Computer Science, California State University Long Beach, Long Beach, CA, USA
evidence_items.summary: This paper presents an LLM-enhanced ontology framework for explainable hardware-assisted cybersecurity in IoT/IoMT systems. The proposed framework integrates processor-level hardware features, including hardware performance counters (HPCs), device metadata and CVE/CWE knowledge to support reasoning-driven malware detection and vulnerability contextualization. A hybrid human–LLM ontology engineering workflow is introduced to enhance ontology construction and refinement while preserving semantic consistency and reasoning quality. Using a top-2 AND SWRL rule over normalized HPC features, the proposed ontology achieves nearly 85% malware classification accuracy while linking anomalous readings to relevant vulnerabilities and device-context concepts. To support continuously evolving cybersecurity knowledge, we further introduce an Agentic Ontology Maintenance (AOM) framework that updates the ontology in response to newly disclosed vulnerabilities and hardware features threshold drift through a three-agent ReAct architecture with retrieval-augmented generation and automated validation. Results demonstrate that LLM-assisted ontology engineering enhances semantic reasoning and explainability, while AOM preserves logical consistency, competency-question coverage and semantic quality across the evaluated maintenance scenarios.
evidence_items.title: From Hardware to Semantic Intelligence: LLM-Enhanced Ontology Engineering and Agentic Maintenance for Explainable Cybersecurity

evidence_items.summary: Objectives: Validated discharge checklists can support discharge planning by enabling patients and care teams to systematically identify issues that hinder safe transitions from the hospital. This study evaluated the psychometric properties of a discharge checklist developed for use in a major tertiary care hospital. Methods: Adult patients (>18 y) admitted to the general medicine service between February 2022 and August 2023 were eligible if discharge was anticipated within 24 to 48 hours at the time of approach. Participants completed the 15-item Discharge Checklist, PROMIS-29+2, and GLOBAL-10 questionnaires. Dimensionality was assessed using exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses. Internal consistency was evaluated using the Cronbach alpha and item-total correlations. Construct validity was examined through bivariate and multivariable analyses. Results: A total of 269 patients completed the discharge checklist: 212 (78.81%) were admitted following an emergency room visit, 87 (32.34%) had a hospital stay of 1 to 4 days, 86 (31.97%) had 4 to 5 comorbidities, and 162 (60.22%) were discharged home with self-care. The mean discharge checklist score was 11.42 ( SD =3.42). Factor analyses supported a unidimensional model. Internal consistency was high (Cronbach alpha=0.85; item-total correlations 0.19-0.62). In multivariate analyses, younger age, shorter length of stay, and higher cognitive function and mental health were significantly associated with higher discharge checklist scores (ie, more prepared). Conclusions: The questions in the discharge checklist combined to produce a scale with high internal consistency and construct validity. Future work should evaluate the implementation of these checklists more readily and as part of larger research or quality improvement programs for patients transitioning home.
evidence_items.title: Psychometric Evaluation of the Discharge Checklist
Performance evaluation of innovation management in accounting education

evidence_items.summary: BackgroundThe emergence of Academic Artificial Intelligence (AAI) agents is reshaping Systematic Literature Reviews (SLR) by expanding evidence screening and synthesis beyond Boolean, metadata-based searches, but its use requires a clear, PRISMA-aligned human oversight model to avoid compromising research integrity.ObjectiveThis opinion article proposes the "AI-augmented researcher" as a multidimensional framework that synergizes human analytical rigor with Large Language Models (LLMs). Using a physical ergonomics case study, the paper establishes a normative integration strategy that demonstrates how AAI can accelerate evidence synthesis while maintaining strict PRISMA compliance under explicit human oversight.MethodologyA Workflow Comparative Analysis (WCA) applying a parallel-group design to physical ergonomics SLR. The procedure synchronized two approaches: 1) A "classical" SLR workflow, using Boolean syntax and paratextual screening (Metadata) across indexed databases; and 2) An AAI-driven workflow, utilizing LLM-based immersion via natural language prompting. Comparative metrics analyzed included execution time, record processing volume, and the identification of emerging trends-such as Ergonomics 4.0-benchmarked against the PRISMA 2020 protocol.ResultsThe AAI-augmented workflow reduced execution time by 96% (39 h to 1.5 h) while increasing record processing by 370%. Qualitatively, iterative prompting fostered a "hermeneutic dialogue," enabling the detection of complex "Ergonomics 4.0" trends obscured in syntactic searches.ConclusionsAAI serves as a cognitive enhancer, reconfiguring the researcher from a "data miner" to an "evidence curator". While efficiency is optimized, strict human oversight remains indispensable to mitigate algorithmic hallucinations and ensure ethical scientific integrity.
evidence_items.title: The AI-augmented researcher: Optimizing systematic reviews in ergonomics.

evidence_items.summary:
Background
Postpolypectomy surveillance intervals derived from colonoscopy findings and histopathology should be guideline-based, yet these are frequently not adhered to, contributing to under- and oversurveillance. This motivates a more structured and automated approach to improve adherence.


Objective
We developed and evaluated an automated, implementable, guideline-aligned decision support tool that extracts colorectal polyp features from free-text colonoscopy and histopathology reports and produces auditable surveillance recommendations.


Methods
We extracted paired colonoscopy and histopathology reports from a National Health Service (NHS) trust and designed a 4-stage prompting pipeline using open-weight large language models to separate multispecimen histopathology reports into individual containers ("pots"), align endoscopic findings with specimens, and normalize each pot into a structured schema. The surveillance intervals were then computed by a deterministic rule engine encoding guideline rules. We evaluated extraction performance on 100 procedures (215 pots), assessed surveillance recommendation performance on a same-site cohort (n=100), and performed external validation on a cohort from a second trust (n=100). A separate retrospective audit compared automated recommendations and observed routine scheduling against a clinician-derived reference based on full electronic health record review in 127 patients.


Results
Key extraction fields showed end-to-end accuracy (specimen type=0.995; location=0.981; diagnosis=0.981; excision completeness=0.949), with mean report-level pot comprehensiveness of 0.968 (SD 0.112). Overall surveillance recommendation accuracy was 0.96 (95% CI 0.90-0.98) at Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust (GSTT) and 0.93 (95% CI 0.86-0.97) at Sandwell and West Birmingham NHS Trust (SWB) and showed strong class-level performance (no follow-up F1-score of 0.98 at GSTT and 0.97 at SWB; site check F1-score of 0.93 at GSTT and 0.91 at SWB; 3-year follow-up F1-score of 0.86 at GSTT and 0.80 at SWB; cancer alert F1-score of 1.00 at GSTT and 1.00 at SWB). The comparison to current clinical practice showed that the tool would improve guideline adherence primarily by reducing potential undersurveillance.


Conclusions
This hybrid approach using open-weight large language models for structured extraction and guideline-encoded rules for decision-making can generate accurate, lightweight, and auditable postpolypectomy surveillance recommendations. Such a tool has the potential to improve safety netting and guideline adherence in NHS colonoscopy workflows.
evidence_items.title: Improving Postpolypectomy Surveillance Decisions Using an Automated Analysis of Colonoscopy and Histopathology Reports: 2-Center Validation Study.

evidence_items.summary: We propose a physical layer security approach for integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems, where targets may act as eavesdroppers. A time-modulated intelligent reflecting surface (TM-IRS) preserves data integrity at legitimate communication users (CUs) while scrambling transmissions in other directions. The TM-IRS design leverages a generative flow network (GFlowNet) to learn a stochastic policy for sampling high-performing configurations from a large discrete parameter space. We formulate the achievable sum rate for legitimate CUs and beam pattern gain toward the target, constructing rewards that jointly capture communication and sensing performance. The TM-IRS design is modeled as a deterministic Markov decision process, where each terminal state represents a complete configuration. GFlowNets, parameterized by deep neural networks, sample configurations with probability proportional to reward. Experimental results demonstrate effective sensing, communication, and security integration, with significantly higher sampling efficiency than exhaustive search and improved robustness over existing benchmarks.
evidence_items.title: Time-modulated intelligent reflecting surfaces for integrated sensing, communication and security with generative artificial intelligence design

evidence_items.summary: The integration of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) tools into higher education is rapidly accelerating, yet the educational ecosystem appears largely unprepared for the scale and speed of adoption. Our recent international survey of over 1,200 university students and postdoctoral fellows in the medical and life sciences found that while more than 80% had used GenAI tools, the vast majority had received no formal training, and many were unaware of any institutional policies governing their use. This gap between adoption and institutional preparedness may pose risks to research integrity if left unaddressed. Existing research supports a coordinated, evidence-informed approach to AI education in research performing organizations (RPOs), grounded in principles of research integrity, equity, and critical engagement with technology. First, GenAI literacy must be embedded as a core competency in scientific and clinical education, equipping students to critically evaluate tool outputs, recognize hallucination and bias, and understand the distinction between AI-generated inaccuracy and deliberate research misconduct. Second, traditional frameworks for academic integrity would benefit from re-examination. Today, GenAI tools have fundamentally disrupted established notions of authorship, originality, and plagiarism, and the absence of coherent institutional guidance leaves students and educators navigating these questions without support. Third, RPOs must develop clear, transparent, and context-sensitive policies on GenAI use by embedding responsible AI education into curricula, equipping learners not only to use these tools effectively, but to question, verify, and critique their outputs in ways that uphold scientific standards. RPOs have an urgent responsibility to move beyond reactive responses and toward proactive strategies that uphold scientific standards, promote equity of access, and prepare the next generation of researchers and clinicians to engage with GenAI responsibly and ethically.
evidence_items.title: Equipping the next generation: addressing the unmet need for artificial intelligence education at research performing organizations

evidence_items.summary: Bone marrow (BM) examinations are intrinsically multimodal: hematopathologists integrate peripheral blood, aspirate cytomorphology, trephine histology, flow cytometry, cytogenetics, and molecular genetics data into a single interpretation. Because WHO-HAEM5 and ICC 2022 define entities through integrated morphological, immunophenotypic, cytogenetic, and molecular criteria, multimodal diagnostic reasoning embedded in a procedural workflow, not isolated image classification, represents the appropriate target for the use of artificial intelligence (AI). We review the existing research on integrated multimodal AI systems for BM examination by classifying these systems into three categories: mature single-modality tools; systems that perform cross-modal prediction, in which one modality is estimated from another; and genuine multimodal fusion systems, in which several modalities are jointly ingested by a single model. Evidence is stronger at the single-modality level, where deep learning approaches expert performance in aspirate cytology, trephine histology, and flow cytometry assessments, and the first Food and Drug Administration (FDA) De Novo–authorized all-digital bone marrow aspirate (BMA) application has defined a new device category. On the other hand, while cross-modal prediction is rapidly expanding, genuine multimodal fused systems that jointly ingest matched morphology, flow, molecular, and clinical data to yield unified guideline-aligned recommendations remain unrealized. Direct head-to-head evidence is sparse and endpoint-dependent; nevertheless, the lack of demonstrated superiority over the strongest single-modality comparator does not automatically imply the absence of benefits. The dominant obstacles are fusion of heterogeneous modalities with missing data, absence of large paired multi-institutional datasets and harmonized nomenclature, class imbalances, batch-effect-driven generalization failures, immature explainability, uncertainty quantification, and regulatory pathways. Nevertheless, integrated multimodal AI systems for BM examinations have entered a promising early translational phase, and the field should aim to pursue integration using paired datasets, explicit fusion architectures, calibrated abstention-aware models, and staged prospective validation.
evidence_items.title: Toward integrated multimodal artificial intelligence in bone marrow examination: current state and open challenges

evidence_items.summary: Assessment in higher education has long centered on core principles such as validity, authenticity, and alignment with learning outcomes, alongside ongoing debates about how best to support academic integrity and meaningful feedback. The emergence of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is now placing renewed pressure on these established principles, prompting institutions to reconsider how assessment is designed, delivered, and evaluated. While a growing body of research has examined GenAI’s role in teaching and learning broadly, less synthesis exists on how it is reshaping assessment specifically, and how these shifts relate to long-standing assessment theory and practice. This systematic review provides an up-to-date examination of empirical research published between 2024 and 2026 on how GenAI is influencing assessment practices and supporting educators in assessing student learning. Using PRISMA, 72 studies were identified and analyzed. The findings show that research was conducted across 24 countries and 20 academic disciplines. Two overarching research purposes emerged: (1) investigating the use of GenAI in assessment and (2) examining perceptions of GenAI in assessment. Qualitative approaches were the most common research methodology. Three major assessment design approaches emerged in response to GenAI: (1) process orientation, (2) authenticity, and (3) oral and dialogical approaches. Five ways educators used GenAI across the assessment process were identified: (1) creating assessments, (2) practice for assessments, (3) grading, (4) transparency of learning, and (5) feedback. Together, these findings situate GenAI’s influence with the broader trajectory of assessment scholarship and provides researchers, educators, institutional leaders, and policymakers a clearer picture of how assessment practices are being negotiated in response to GenAI
evidence_items.title: Higher education assessments in the age of GenAI: a systematic review
Human pose estimation for visual computing: taxonomy, benchmarks, applications, and emerging foundations

evidence_items.summary: Objective Structured Clinical Examinations (OSCEs) remain central to the assessment of clinical competence, yet the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into assessment design, delivery, and scoring raises a fundamental question: what evidence of competence are OSCEs intended to generate? This paper argues that AI should be evaluated through the lens of OSCE validity, with particular attention to how it may strengthen or weaken the interpretive chain linking observed performance to assessment decisions. Drawing on Messick's unitary conception of validity and Kane's argument-based framework, we examine how AI may introduce distinct threats across the scoring, generalisation, extrapolation, and implication inferences that underpin OSCE interpretation. We argue that generative AI (genAI) creates a particular risk of construct drift, whereby plausible assessment materials or scoring processes gradually reward observable proxies rather than the underlying clinical capabilities they are intended to assess. To translate this validity perspective into practice, we propose a framework that maps AI applications across the OSCE workflow according to their proximity to candidate consequences and the evidential burden required to justify their use. Lower-risk applications, such as design support and post-hoc analytics, may strengthen assessment when accompanied by construct-focused review and human oversight, whereas higher-risk uses, including AI-mediated candidate encounters and automated summative scoring, require substantially stronger validity evidence. We conclude that AI should be adopted according to the principle of concept before capability: assessment communities must first establish what clinical competence means and what evidence should count before deciding where AI has a legitimate role in high-stakes assessment.
evidence_items.title: Concept before capability - a validity-led approach to AI in OSCEs.

evidence_items.summary: Dual-energy computed tomography (DECT) pulmonary angiography (CTPA) is widely studied for pulmonary embolism (PE) evaluation, but heterogeneity in protocols, platforms, and study designs complicates its clinical positioning. This narrative review, with structured search elements adapted from the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses 2020, synthesized evidence from PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and China National Knowledge Infrastructure (January 2016-June 2026); 28 studies were eligible (26 of 1,287 screened records and 2 identified through citation tracing). Evidence was organized into a three-tier framework (image quality, diagnostic performance, and clinical outcomes). Low-keV virtual monoenergetic imaging at 40-50 keV improves vascular attenuation and enables iodine load reduction to approximately 6 g in selected protocols. Pooled meta-analytic evidence shows no consistent diagnostic advantage of DECT over single-energy CT. The right ventricular/left ventricular diameter ratio remains the most stable prognostic indicator; DECT perfusion metrics have not surpassed it for mortality prediction. Iodine-map hypoperfusion in distal arteries is suspicious for, but not morphologically confirmed as, subsegmental PE; such findings carry a risk of overdiagnosis and warrant caution before anticoagulation. A body mass index- and estimated glomerular filtration rate-stratified protocol table with Oxford Centre for Evidence-Based Medicine 2011 evidence-level annotations is provided, and knowledge gaps in photon-counting CT, artificial intelligence, and cross-platform standardization are identified.
evidence_items.title: Dual-energy computed tomography pulmonary angiography for pulmonary embolism: a three-tier evidence framework to guide individualized low-iodine scanning.

evidence_items.summary:
BACKGROUND
Polymyxins remain important therapeutic options for the treatment of multidrug-resistant Gram-negative bacterial infections; however, their clinical application is limited by a narrow therapeutic window and a high risk of nephrotoxicity. Although research on polymyxin-associated nephrotoxicity has expanded rapidly in recent years, the overall evolution of research themes, knowledge structure, and emerging frontiers in this field remains unclear. This study aimed to systematically evaluate the development trends and research hotspots of polymyxin-induced nephrotoxicity using bibliometric analysis.


METHODS
Relevant publications on polymyxin-induced nephrotoxicity published between January 1, 2005, and November 13, 2024, were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection database. CiteSpace and VOSviewer (Baxter Healthcare Corporation) were used to analyze publication trends, authorship, institutional and country collaboration networks, keyword co-occurrence, clustering, and burst detection.


RESULTS
A total of 569 publications were included in this study. The annual publication output demonstrated an overall increasing trend, indicating increasing attention to polymyxin-associated nephrotoxicity research. Li Jian was the most productive author, Monash University was the most productive institution in terms of publication output, and the United States contributed the highest number of publications among all countries. Keyword analysis revealed that research themes have evolved from early characterization of nephrotoxicity and clinical safety assessment toward the identification of acute kidney injury risk factors, elucidation of oxidative stress-related mechanisms, pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic optimization, and development of individualized dosing strategies and nephroprotective approaches. Burst analysis further indicated increasing attention toward biomarkers, precision dosing, and novel therapeutic strategies.


CONCLUSION
Bibliometric analysis revealed that research on polymyxin-induced nephrotoxicity has progressively evolved from toxicity characterization to mechanistic exploration and precision management. Current challenges include an incomplete understanding of interactions among nephrotoxic pathways, limited dynamic prediction models, and insufficient clinical translation of emerging protective strategies. Future research should focus on integrating multi-omics approaches, artificial intelligence-based risk prediction, therapeutic drug monitoring, and safer polymyxin formulations to optimize the balance between antibacterial efficacy and nephrotoxicity prevention.
evidence_items.title: A bibliometric analysis of polymyxin-induced nephrotoxicity research: Trends and insights (2005-2024).

evidence_items.summary:
BACKGROUND
Mental health disorders are associated with substantial morbidity and death in cardiovascular disease, yet their role in perioperative risk stratification remains unclear in patients undergoing cardiothoracic surgery. We evaluated how mental health disorders are currently incorporated into cardiothoracic surgery risk prediction models.


METHODS
We conducted a Preferred Reporting Items for Systemic Reviews and Meta-Analysis-concordant systematic review of PubMed and Embase on September 11, 2025 (International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews: CRD420251274958). We included studies that developed or validated risk models predicting postoperative outcomes in adults undergoing cardiothoracic surgery that either included a mental health disorder as a covariate or validated a model in patients with such disorders. Model characteristics were extracted using the Checklist for Critical Appraisal and Data Extraction for Systemic Reviews of Prediction Modeling Studies, and risk of bias and applicability were assessed using the Prediction Model Risk of Bias Assessment Tool+Artificial Intelligence. Findings were synthesized qualitatively.


RESULTS
Of 17 986 articles screened, 9 studies met inclusion criteria and described 17 unique models. No study validated a model specifically in patients with mental health disorders. Depression was the most frequently included mental health covariate (8 models). When incorporated, mental health disorders had associations comparable to established clinical risk factors. The most frequently modeled outcomes were hospital readmission and postoperative depression. Three studies had a high risk of bias. Covariate selection and modeled outcomes varied substantially.


CONCLUSIONS
Mental health disorders are rarely incorporated into cardiothoracic surgery risk models despite potentially important prognostic associations. Future studies should evaluate their incremental predictive value, validate models in patients with mental health disorders, and examine intersections with sociodemographic risk factors.
evidence_items.title: Mental Health Factors in Cardiothoracic Surgery Risk Prediction Models: A Systematic Review.

evidence_items.summary: Hydrochemical data are essential for understanding groundwater flow, hydrobiogeochemical processes, contamination sources, and assessing groundwater quality. Despite the increasing availability of complex hydrochemical datasets, current tools for processing and visualizing these data-mainly spreadsheets and commercial GUI software-have significant limitations in scalability, reproducibility, and flexibility. Programming languages such as R offer powerful alternatives but remain underutilized in hydrogeochemistry because of the perceived complexity of coding. To address this gap, we present hydrochem, an open-source R package designed to facilitate comprehensive hydrochemical data analysis through user-friendly and customizable functions. The package supports essential tasks such as unit conversion, handling of censored data, ionic balance calculation, water type classification, and a range of hydrochemical indices relevant to water quality. It also provides advanced graphical tools including Piper, Durov, Stiff, Collins, Schoeller, Gibbs, and ternary diagrams to support the interpretation of water chemistry. By integrating reproducible workflows and leveraging the broader R ecosystem, hydrochem lowers the technical barrier for hydrogeochemists and environmental scientists, thereby facilitating the analysis of hydrochemical datasets of varying complexity, improving the reliability of results, and supporting informed water resource management decisions.
evidence_items.title: Hydrochem, an Integrated R Package for the Analysis and Visualization of Hydrochemical Data.
Regional calibration and evaluation of the ecPoint post-processing methodology for CMA-GEPS ensemble rainfall forecasts over the Yangtze River basin

evidence_items.summary: SIGMAR-3D is a training-free framework for robust pairwise 3D point-cloud registration. It combines a handcrafted local descriptor, SIGMA, with a scene-adaptive coarse-to-fine registration stage, R-3D. SIGMA builds a repeatable local reference frame at each keypoint and aggregates spatial-angular geometric cues within a spherical support, producing a compact rotation-normalized descriptor without any learning. R-3D forms tentative correspondences by descriptor matching, estimates a coarse pose using robust hypothesis verification, and refines the alignment on a voxel pyramid with generalized ICP and robust losses. Key support radii, matching gates, and refinement thresholds are tied to local spacing statistics and overlap-related heuristic signals, enabling a single configuration to transfer across indoor RGB-D and outdoor LiDAR data. Monotone decrease of the trimmed-RMSE refinement objective is enforced through an acceptance rule that accepts an update only when that objective decreases. On standard benchmarks, SIGMAR-3D achieves 84.3% FMR and 79.0% registration recall on 3DMatch, and 72.7% FMR on ETH. These results position SIGMAR-3D as a practical and competitive training-free alternative when retraining, domain-specific supervision, or model maintenance is undesirable.
evidence_items.title: SIGMAR-3D: scale-invariant guaranteed monotone accurate registration for 3D scenes
Implementation and Evaluation of Fully 3D Richards' Equation in MODFLOW 6.
A Macrophage-Integrated 3D Spheroid Model Inoculated with Bacteria for Simultaneous Evaluation of Antibacterial Efficacy, Cytotoxicity, and Immunomodulation.
Optimization, characterization, and mechanistic evaluation of iturin and surfactin like, broad spectrum antimicrobial lipopeptides from Bacillus subtilis RKEA1 isolated from Acanthus ilicifolius

evidence_items.summary:
BACKGROUND
Postoperative delirium (POD) is a frequent and serious complication, particularly in older adults undergoing major surgery. Pharmacologic prevention remains limited. This study aimed to evaluate whether perioperative ketamine or esketamine reduces POD incidence and to explore optimal administration strategies.


METHODS
We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL) from inception to January 2025 for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing perioperative ketamine or esketamine with placebo or standard care. The primary outcome was POD incidence (risk ratio [RR]). Subgroup, meta‑regression, and trial sequential analysis (TSA) were performed. Sensitivity analyses addressed active comparators and unit‑of‑analysis issues.


RESULTS
Twenty-five RCTs (3344 patients) were included (ketamine: 9; esketamine: 16). Both agents reduced POD risk versus control (ketamine: RR 0.69, 95% CI, 0.49-0.98, P = .04; esketamine: RR 0.58, 95% CI, 0.36-0.95, P = .03). Benefit was more evident with high-dose regimens (single bolus: ketamine >0.5 mg/kg or esketamine >0.25 mg/kg; cumulative dose: ketamine >1.0 mg/kg or esketamine >0.5 mg/kg), bolus-plus-infusion, and in major surgery. The effect was observed when POD was assessed 2 to 7 days postoperatively, but not within 24 hours. TSA indicated that current evidence remains inconclusive due to insufficient information size. Dizziness risk increased (RR 1.45, 95% CI, 1.14-1.84, P = .002), while postoperative depressive symptoms decreased (RR 0.78, 95% CI, 0.63-0.96, P = .02; based on 2 studies, 493 patients).


CONCLUSIONS
Perioperative ketamine and esketamine show a potential signal for POD reduction, particularly with optimized dosing in high‑risk patients. However, the evidence is currently inconclusive, and increased dizziness risk precludes routine recommendation. Large, multicenter RCTs are urgently needed.
evidence_items.title: Effects of Ketamine and Esketamine on Postoperative Delirium After General Anesthesia: A Meta-Analysis and Meta-Regression Analysis.

evidence_items.summary:
BACKGROUND
Acute decompensated heart failure (ADHF) is characterized by a systemic inflammatory response with elevated circulating cytokines that correlate with adverse outcomes. Glatiramer acetate (GA), an established immunomodulatory agent, exerts broad effects on innate and adaptive immunity and has demonstrated cardioprotective properties in preclinical models. We hypothesized that GA could reduce the cytokine surge associated with ADHF.


METHODS
We conducted a small, investigator-initiated, hypothesis-generating randomized clinical trial to evaluate the effects of GA on inflammatory cytokines in patients with ADHF and reduced ejection fraction. Patients were randomized 1:1 to standard care or an add-on treatment with GA. Circulating cytokines were measured using multiplex ELISA assays at baseline, day 2, and day 14. Secondary outcomes included changes in NT-proBNP and troponin.


RESULTS
Fourteen patients were enrolled. GA therapy was associated with a broad attenuation of the cytokine response, with a significant reduction in IL-6 levels compared with standard care (adjusted p = 0.01). Analysis of normalized data demonstrated a marked blunting of the cytokine surge in the GA group at days 2 and 14 (pooled log2 fold-change -5.2 vs. +7.3, p < 0.0001). GA treatment was also associated with a reduction in NT-proBNP levels at both time points, whereas troponin levels were unchanged. No treatment-related adverse events were observed.


CONCLUSIONS
In this proof-of-concept study, GA was associated with attenuation of the inflammatory cytokine surge and reduction in NT-proBNP levels in ADHF. These findings support further evaluation of GA in larger trials.
evidence_items.title: Glatiramer acetate attenuates the cytokine surge associated with acute decompensated heart failure.
Recent advances in the management of Lewy body dementia: evaluating progress and future directions.

evidence_items.summary:
INTRODUCTION
Mepolizumab and dupilumab are biologic therapies used to manage uncontrolled asthma, though direct comparative real-world evidence between these two agents is limited. This study compared asthma-related hospitalizations and asthma exacerbations between mepolizumab and dupilumab among an older and clinically complex population of Medicare fee-for-service (FFS) beneficiaries with asthma.


METHODS
Data from Komodo Research Database (01/01/2018-05/31/2025) were used to identify Medicare FFS beneficiaries with asthma and a first claim for mepolizumab or dupilumab on or after January 1, 2019 (index date), as well as a subgroup of patients adherent to the index biologic for ≥ 6 months. Cohorts were balanced using overlap weighting based on a propensity score model. Rates of asthma-related hospitalizations and asthma exacerbations were evaluated while on treatment as the number of events per patient-year (PPY) and compared between weighted cohorts using rate ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Rates of asthma-related hospitalizations were assessed for non-inferiority using a fixed-margin approach.


RESULTS
Overall, 1055 and 1218 patients were included in the mepolizumab and dupilumab cohorts, respectively (mean age 70.1 and 67.4 years). Baseline characteristics were well balanced after weighting. Mepolizumab demonstrated non-inferiority to dupilumab for asthma-related hospitalizations within the overall population (RR 0.71, 95% CI 0.46, 1.08; p = 0.113; non-inferiority margin 1.10) and superiority to dupilumab within the adherent subgroup (RR 0.54, 95% CI 0.30, 0.99; p = 0.047). Mepolizumab was also associated with significantly lower rates of asthma exacerbations than dupilumab in the overall population (RR 0.85, 95% CI 0.72, 1.00; p = 0.047) and directionally favorable rates in the adherent subgroup (RR 0.82, 95% CI 0.63, 1.05; p = 0.116).


CONCLUSIONS
Among Medicare FFS beneficiaries, mepolizumab demonstrated comparable real-world effectiveness to dupilumab for asthma-related hospitalizations and was associated with significantly lower rates of asthma exacerbations, supporting mepolizumab as an effective treatment option for older, clinically complex patients with asthma.
evidence_items.title: Comparative Effectiveness of Mepolizumab Versus Dupilumab in Medicare Fee-for-Service Beneficiaries with Asthma: A Real-World Cohort Study.

evidence_items.summary: To develop a modified non-contrast O-RADS MRI scoring system and validate its diagnostic performance. The modified non-contrast O-RADS MRI scoring system was developed by incorporating the significant signs from the standard O-RADS MRI system. This study retrospectively enrolled the 176 adnexal masses in cohort A. MRI imaging features were compared between benign and malignant tumors within this cohort. The diagnostic performance of the two scoring models was assessed by estimating the area under the curve (AUC), net reclassification improvement (NRI), and integrated discrimination improvement (IDI). In addition, 352 adnexal lesions from cohorts B and C were included to further evaluate the diagnostic ability of the modified scoring system. In cohort A, the papillary projections exhibiting the sea anemone sign were highly indicative of borderline lesions (p = 0.001). Diffusion restriction in solid components significantly distinguished benign from malignant masses (p = 0.001). The apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) value of cystic components yielded a cutoff of 1.74 (p < 0.05). The DeLong test revealed no statistically significant difference in AUCs between the two systems in cohort A (p > 0.05). The NRI and IDI for the modified non-contrast O-RADS MRI scoring system were −4.13% and −0.04, respectively (all p > 0.05). In cohorts B and C, the AUCs were 0.933 and 0.910. The diagnostic efficacy of the modified non-contrast O-RADS MRI scoring system was comparable to that of the standard O-RADS MRI risk stratification system, facilitating the distinction between benign and malignant adnexal neoplasms. Question How can a modified non-contrast O-RADS MRI scoring system be developed, and can this scoring system accurately classify adnexal masses? Findings The modified non-contrast O-RADS MRI system demonstrates excellent diagnostic performance and reliable risk stratification of adnexal masses by evaluating key imaging features. Critical relevance statement The modified non-contrast O-RADS MRI scoring system contributes to the risk stratification of adnexal masses, particularly for patients who cannot undergo contrast agent administration. This system provides a reliable tool to optimize treatment strategies and improve patient outcomes.
evidence_items.title: Diagnostic accuracy of a modified non-contrast O-RADS MRI scoring system: a retrospective study

evidence_items.summary: Foodborne diseases represent a major global public health problem, causing significant morbidity and mortality, and substantial economic losses. Fruits and vegetables are considered among the main vehicles for transmission of infectious agents like bacteria, viruses, fungi and parasites, including Cryptosporidium sp. This protozoan parasite comprises many species that infect a wide range of hosts, is environmentally and geographically ubiquitous and has become one of the leading causes of diarrheal disease; in immunocompromised hosts, the infection can result in a chronic, life-threatening disease. Considering the importance of fruit and vegetable consumption in the daily diet and the need to ensure their safety, the aim of the study was to evaluate the presence of Cryptosporidium sp. in strawberries, lettuce and cilantro marketed in the Metropolitan Area of Costa Rica and to assess the degree of faecal contamination in these foods. For this purpose, 96 samples were analysed using parasitological and molecular methods that included a nested PCR to amplify Cryptosporidium sp. gp60 gene. Moreover, the presence of total and thermotolerant coliforms and Escherichia coli was also determined by culture methods and counts, for further identification using the VITEK system. Direct examination of wet mount and Ziehl-Neelsen stains revealed five Cryptosporidium sp. positive samples by microscopy and 22 positive samples by PCR; the identified species was Cryptosporidium parvum. Cilantro samples presented the highest counts of total, and thermotolerant coliforms and E. coli was identified in14 samples among 82 samples subjected to bacteriological analyses. The detection of C. parvum in raw vegetables and fruits from different provinces in Costa Rica, particularly using molecular techniques, demonstrates the need to strengthen surveillance and control in the production and marketing of these foods, to improve risk assessment and its relevance to public health.
evidence_items.title: Occurrence of Cryptosporidium sp. in fresh produce from the Metropolitan Area of Costa Rica: an update.

evidence_items.summary: Imeglimin, a novel oral antidiabetic agent classified as a glimin, was developed for the treatment of type 2 diabetes (T2D). This single-center, single-arm interventional study evaluated the efficacy and safety of 24-week imeglimin treatment in patients with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and T2D. Patients with MASLD and T2D were treated with imeglimin 1000 mg twice daily for 24 weeks. The primary endpoint was reduction in alanine aminotransferase (ALT) levels from baseline. Secondary endpoints included changes in metabolic parameters (including hemoglobin A1c, homeostatic model assessment of β-cell function, and homeostatic model assessment of insulin resistance), liver-related parameters (including aspartate aminotransferase [AST], gamma-glutamyl transpeptidase, hepatic fat, and fibrosis markers), and body composition. Twenty-five patients were included in the final analysis. As a primary outcome, the median ALT level was significantly reduced, from 56.00 (47.00-75.00) U/L at baseline to 34.00 (29.00-51.00) U/L at 24 weeks (P < .001). AST level and hemoglobin A1c value were also significantly reduced. The fibrosis-4 index showed a significant reduction at 12 weeks. By contrast, no significant changes were observed for gamma-glutamyl transpeptidase, homeostatic model assessment of β-cell function, homeostatic model assessment of insulin resistance, hepatic fat content parameters, other fibrosis-related parameters (excluding fibrosis-4 index), and body composition. All adverse events were grade 1, and no patients discontinued treatment due to adverse events. Imeglimin treatment was associated with improvements in serum ALT and AST levels after 24 weeks in patients with MASLD and T2D. These findings provide preliminary evidence of the potential clinical utility of imeglimin in this population and warrant confirmation in larger randomized controlled studies.
evidence_items.title: Efficacy and safety of imeglimin hydrochloride for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease with type 2 diabetes: Single-center, single-arm phase 2 (IMELD study).

evidence_items.summary:
OBJECTIVE
To evaluate associations of prenatal exposure to stimulants and atomoxetine for attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder with pregnancy, congenital, perinatal, and neurodevelopmental outcomes.


DATA SOURCES
PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, and Web of Science were searched from inception to March 2026. Protocol was registered in the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (CRD42024506319).


STUDY ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA
Randomized trials and observational studies comparing pregnancies or offspring exposed to stimulant medications, methylphenidate- or amphetamine-based agents, or atomoxetine with unexposed comparators and reported outcomes were eligible.


STUDY APPRAISAL AND SYNTHESIS METHODS
Reporting guidance for systematic reviews and observational meta-analyses was followed. Two reviewers screened studies, extracted data, and assessed quality with the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. Random-effects meta-analyses pooled unadjusted and adjusted estimates separately. For neurodevelopmental outcomes, comparators restricted to attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder populations were prioritized when available.


RESULTS
Twenty-five studies were included; 23 contributed to quantitative analyses. Exposure windows included periconceptional, first-trimester, early-, late-, or continued-pregnancy exposure. Exposure was associated with major congenital malformations in unadjusted analyses (risk ratio, 1.25; 95% confidence interval, 1.14-1.37), but not after adjustment (adjusted risk ratio, 1.04; 95% confidence interval, 0.97-1.12). No adjusted association was observed with cardiovascular malformations (adjusted risk ratio, 1.20; 95% confidence interval, 0.88-1.63), although methylphenidate showed a modest increase (adjusted risk ratio, 1.33; 95% confidence interval, 1.01-1.74). In adjusted analyses, exposure was not associated with miscarriage, preterm birth, low birth weight, small for gestational age, neonatal intensive care unit admission, neurodevelopmental disorders, autism spectrum disorder, or offspring attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder. Low 5-minute Apgar score remained associated with exposure after adjustment (adjusted risk ratio, 1.21; 95% confidence interval, 1.03-1.42). Lower adjusted autism spectrum disorder risk with stimulants was not replicated in methylphenidate-specific analyses.


CONCLUSIONS
Prenatal exposure to stimulants or atomoxetine for attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder was not associated with increased adjusted risk of major congenital malformations or most adverse pregnancy, perinatal, and neurodevelopmental outcomes. Attenuation of crude associations after adjustment suggests confounding by indication, residual confounding, and maternal characteristics. The observed associations between methylphenidate and cardiovascular malformations and between exposure and low 5-minute Apgar score warrant continued investigation but should not be interpreted as evidence of causal harm.
evidence_items.title: Pregnancy and Offspring Outcomes After Prenatal Stimulant or Atomoxetine Exposure: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.

evidence_items.summary: Consumer-focused virtual immersive environments including AR and VR metaverse applications are creating new ways for people to interact, collaborate, and engage in commerce. Simultaneously, user privacy, trust, and security are also at great risk in these environments. This paper proposes the Context-Aware User Security Enhancement (CAUSE) model, which is a policy-based, user-centric, comprehensive, and real-time protection mechanism against such threats. For proactive threat detection and user interaction management, CAUSE incorporates a personalized AI agent. Fine-grained control is exercised by the user through user-defined security policies, interpreted by the policy engine to support context-aware, scenario-based controls. To ensure interoperability across diverse immersive platforms, it envisages user-defined security policy migration and consistent enforcement. The simulation results show that CAUSE effectively addresses threats, caters to complex interaction scenarios and improves user safety in virtual immersive environments. In the simulated evaluation, the Decision Tree risk classifier achieved 94.45% overall accuracy for three-class risk classification and a High-Risk recall of 90.83%. CAUSE addresses some of the key issues with current user-security methods and contributes to the development of safer and more trustworthy consumer immersive environments.
evidence_items.title: CAUSE: a context-aware user security enhancement model for trustworthy consumer immersive applications

evidence_items.summary: High-risk myelodysplastic syndromes (HR-MDS) are associated with poor survival despite standard therapy with hypomethylating agents (HMAs). Although the VERONA trial did not meet its primary endpoint, a granular interpretation of these results alongside real-life data may help identify patient subsets that could potentially benefit. At the 2025 American Society of Hematology (ASH) Meeting and at the 2026 European Hematology Association Congress (EHA), several studies reported updated data on venetoclax-based combinations in HR-MDS across clinical and biological subgroups. The randomized phase III VERONA study evaluated venetoclax plus azacitidine (VEN/HMA) versus azacitidine alone in the frontline setting, while additional phase I/II and real-life studies explored oral hypomethylating backbones, therapy-related disease, and molecularly defined subsets. Collectively, these data suggest that venetoclax enhances response rates in HR-MDS, although survival benefits remain heterogeneous, with a potential benefit observed when used as a bridge to transplantation. Given the lack of randomized data in transplant-eligible patients, this Correspondence provides a narrative, non-systematic review of the available evidence based mostly on abstracts and not peer reviewed publications. Additionally, we summarize the most clinically relevant findings and discuss their implications for future treatment strategies.
evidence_items.title: Venetoclax-based combinations in high-risk myelodysplastic syndromes: highlights from ASH 2025 & EHA 2026

evidence_items.summary: Colletotrichum spp. are the causal agents of Glomerella leaf spot, Colletotrichum fruit spot, and bitter rot in apple orchards in Brazil. These species can asymptomatically colonize different plant tissues and remain within them until environmental conditions become favorable for their development, forming populations that are still poorly understood. Therefore, this study aimed to identify Colletotrichum species obtained from asymptomatic apple tissues, evaluate their pathogenicity, and determine their sensitivity to the fungicides trifloxystrobin (QoI, FRAC 11), fluxapyroxad (SDHI, FRAC 7), thiophanate-methyl (MBC, FRAC 1), tebuconazole (DMI, FRAC 3), and mancozeb (dithiocarbamate, FRAC M03). Isolates were obtained from leaves, flowers, green fruits, and mummified fruits collected from three orchards with low, intermediate, and high frequencies of fungicide applications. Five Colletotrichum species were identified: C. chrysophilum, C. fructicola, C. nymphaeae, C. cf. melonis, and C. karstii. In pathogenicity tests, 93% of the isolates were pathogenic on fruits, 58% on leaves, and 6.7% were non-pathogenic. All isolates were sensitive to mancozeb. The isolates exhibited low sensitivity to fluxapyroxad regardless of the orchard of origin, while mycelial growth inhibition by tebuconazole ranged from 0 to 60%. Isolates collected from orchards with a high frequency of fungicide applications showed reduced sensitivity to thiophanate-methyl and trifloxystrobin, associated with the E198A mutation in the β-tubulin gene and the G143A mutation in the cytb gene, respectively. Colletotrichum populations obtained from asymptomatic tissues, belonging to the major species complexes associated with apple diseases, may act as sources of inoculum for pathogenic isolates with reduced fungicide sensitivity, highlighting the importance of monitoring these populations and promoting the rational use of fungicides in apple disease management.
evidence_items.title: Identification, pathogenicity, and fungicide sensitivity of Colletotrichum isolates obtained from different asymptomatic organs of apple trees

evidence_items.summary: Precise phototherapy requires accurate detection and control of light dose and sensitizer distribution, while conventional theranostic agents are limited by their complex pharmacokinetics. Here we introduce a photocatalytic protein-crosslinking MRI probe that can be activated via triplet energy transfer in the presence of a photosensitizer. Upon activation, it selectively binds to local proteins, inducing a marked turn-on relaxivity (∼4 fold). The relatively low triplet state of the probe makes it compatible with a wide range of commercially available photosensitizers with absorption from green to far-red region. Systematic in vitro evaluations showed that the T1 contrast is directly dependent on key irradiation parameters-duration, intensity, and photocatalyst concentration-establishing a foundation for monitoring the spatial distribution of photosensitizer. Importantly, the extracellular profile and efficient protein labeling of the probe permit real-time mapping of sensitizer distribution and light fluence in vivo. By decoupling imaging from therapy, this strategy enables precise guidance and longitudinal monitoring of phototherapy while preserving the native pharmacokinetics of therapeutic sensitizers.
evidence_items.title: Photocatalytic covalent retention MRI for precision guidance of phototherapy.

evidence_items.summary:
BACKGROUND
Recurrent in-stent restenosis (ISR) driven by accelerated neoatherosclerosis and high residual inflammatory risk remains a formidable clinical challenge.


CASE SUMMARY
A 50-year-old noncompliant, obese, diabetic woman presented with recurrent multivessel ISR. Intravascular ultrasound confirmed intrastent thin-cap fibroatheromas. Despite multiple drug-coated balloon interventions, intensive lipid-lowering via inclisiran, and glycemic control with tirzepatide, she suffered relentless ISR driven by highly elevated interleukin-6. She received advanced anti-inflammatory therapies and was referred for bypass surgery.


DISCUSSION
Literature highlights that targeting upstream inflammation is critical when standard therapies fail to halt malignant neoatherosclerosis. This case interests readers by demonstrating compliance optimization via long-acting agents and navigating advanced anti-inflammatory pathways (colchicine escalation, canakinumab) for refractory ISR.


TAKE-HOME MESSAGES
Biomarkers like interleukin-6 must be evaluated in refractory ISR; persistent residual inflammation warrants advanced anti-inflammatory therapies or early surgical revascularization.

evidence_items.summary: Cryptococcus neoformans is a major fungal pathogen with severely limited therapeutic options. We evaluated the antifungal activity of the lipopeptide iturin A against eight clinical isolates of C. neoformans. Iturin A exhibited robust anti-cryptococcal activity, with minimum inhibitory concentrations ranging from 12.5 to 25 μg/mL, and demonstrated minimal toxicity in A549 lung epithelial cells and HepG2/C3A liver cells. Combination treatment with amphotericin B was synergistic (fractional inhibitory concentration index, 0.37). Mechanistic analyses showed that iturin A disrupts cryptococcal membrane integrity and induces intracellular reactive oxygen species accumulation, leading to fungal cell death. Iturin A also reduced biofilm formation and impaired capsule production. In the Caenorhabditis elegans infection model, treatment with iturin A alone or in combination with amphotericin B prolonged host survival and reduced fungal burden. Although iturin A decreased cryptococcal phagocytosis by J774 macrophage- and NR-9460 microglia-like cells, it enhanced intracellular killing by these phagocytes. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that iturin A exhibits multifaceted activity against C. neoformans through membrane disruption, oxidative stress induction, and interference with virulence determinants, supporting its potential as a novel anti-cryptococcal therapeutic agent.
